name: Callable type kinds and signature compatibility use the errata rules

input.source_text: class A { public fun f(x: Integer) -> Integer { x } } module M { public fun run() -> Object { let m = Reflection::Class.method(A, :f); let mismatched = try { let bad: BoundMethod<(Integer) -> Integer> = { |x: Integer| -> Integer x }; bad } catch e { e }; let bound = m.bind(A.new()); let closure: Closure<(Integer) -> Integer> = { |x: Integer| -> Integer x }; [mismatched, bound.call(5), closure.call(7)] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C018 is superseded by C094 and C096: the callable Type now NAMES its kind as Closure<S> or BoundMethod<S>, and signature compatibility is checked at the call site rather than by variance. Both halves are observable. Kind is enforced, so a Closure assigned to BoundMethod<S> fails and the reverse fails too, which C096's invariance requires; and once the kind matches, both remain ordinary callables invoked at the call site. The signature half stays static by design under C096, so this row observes the kind rule and the call, which is what the clause actually fixes.
